 Order
This matter is taken up through hybrid arrangement (virtual/physical) mode.

2. The petitioner by filing this writ petition has prayed as under:
"to admit the Writ application, issue notice to the Opp.parties, call for the lower court records and entering into the facts, records/orders and provision of the National Highways Act, 1956 as well as The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, quash the impugned order dtd.23.06.2022 under Annexure-7 and issue an appropriate writ directing the opp. parties to disburse the actual legitimate dues @ Rs.70 lakhs per acre with @ 12%
interest in favour of the petitioner".
3.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Additional Standing Counsel.

4. Perusal of the averments taken in the writ petition as also the documents annexed thereto, reveals that in respect of the acquired land, the Opposite Party No.1 had earlier passed an award on 31.10.2015 in terms of provision of National Highways Act, // 2 // 1956 (in short the NH Act) and that was questioned by the petitioner by filing an application under section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (in short the AC Act) before the learned District Judge, Puri, which was registered as Arbitration Misc. Case No.20 of 2016.
The order dated 19.12.2017 passed by the learned District Judge, Puri in the aforesaid Case was challenged before this Court in ARBA No.22 of 2018.
This Court disposed of the Appeal by remitting the matter to the Arbitrator to revisit the question of valuation of petitioner's land which has been acquired and pass an award afresh.

Challenging the order passed by this Court in ARBA No.22 of 2018, the petitioner filed Special Leave Petition (Civil) Diary No.2018 of 2023 before the Supreme Court which has been dismissed on 21.03.2023.

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) Diary No.2018 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: In the meantime, the Opposite Party No.1 has again passed the award on 23.06.2022.

If the petitioner wants to question the award, he is required under the law to file an application under section 34 of AC Act before the learned District Judge having the jurisdiction and thereafter he can approach this Court in challenging that order of the District Judge by filing an appeal, as provided under section 37 of AC Act.

5. The above being position, we find out the move to question the award passed on 23.06.2022 by the Collector, Puri as at Annexure-7 by filing this writ petition is not entertainable.
6.
Accordingly, the writ petition stands dismissed.
